record.question: A client experiencing a panic attack keeps repeating, "I'm dying, I can't breathe.". What action by the nurse should be most therapeutic initially?
options: Encouraging the client to take slow, deep breaths
Verbalizing mild disapproval of the anxious behavior
Asking the client what he means when he says "I am dying."
Offering an explanation about why the symptoms are occurring
record.explanation: Answer A: Encouraging the client to take slow, deep breaths. During acute panic, remain with the patient, use a calm approach, and guide slow breathing/grounding; explanation and exploration are more helpful after distress decreases. Source/context note: Do not force deep breathing; coach gentle, paced breathing and assess for medical causes of dyspnea. Reference: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK430973/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
